chapter_title: Chương 68: 0068【Khám phá bất ngờ của phóng viên Trần】

segments.title: Chương 68: 0068【Khám phá bất ngờ của phóng viên Trần】
segments.content:
Afternoon.

Stopping the car not far from the town market bridge, Chen Feng rolled down his window and asked a fruit stall owner, "How do I get to the Township Central School?"

"Just go up that slope."

With the Spring Festival approaching, business at the fruit stall was good. The owner enthusiastically solicited, "Boss, are you going to visit relatives? The fruit here is very fresh. Look at these Red Fuji apples, a new variety, big, crisp, and sweet…"

Chen Feng had no intention of buying fruit. He casually asked, "Do you know Chen Guiliang?"

The stall owner laughed, "Of course I do."

"Is he very famous?" Chen Feng sensed there was more to the story and quickly got out of the car to offer the owner a cigarette.

But the stall owner became wary. He avoided talking about Chen Guiliang and instead praised the cigarette, "Jiaozi, good smokes."

Chen Feng simply handed over the half-empty pack, "Are you a relative of Chen Guiliang?"

This time, the stall owner didn't take the cigarettes. "What are you asking about him for?"

Chen Feng fabricated a story, "I'm a teacher from No. 2 High School, here to do a home visit during the winter break."

The stall owner smiled but said nothing more.

He wasn't an idiot. It was two days before the New Year, how could a teacher possibly be doing a home visit?

Chen Feng was out of options and had to pull out his own press card. "I'm a reporter from the West China Metropolis Daily. Chen Guiliang has become famous, and I'm here to interview him."

The stall owner stared at the press card for a long time, his suspicion only growing.

Chen Feng then took a newspaper from his car and showed his own ID card. "Look at the reporter's name on this article here. Isn't it the same as the one on my ID card and press card?"

The stall owner finally smiled. "Chen Guiliang is a good student, a very good one."

"How is he good?" Chen Feng asked.

The stall owner didn't go into detail, only repeating, "He's just a good student, you should write an article to praise him."

Chen Feng pressed further, "What good deeds has he done?"

The stall owner hemmed and hawed, saying nothing.

Chen Feng said, "If you don't know, I'll go interview someone else."

The stall owner finally spoke, but not about Chen Guiliang. "Over there by the market is Baishaba Village. There's a son of a bitch in the village who came back from working in the south and started a 'Green Dragon Gang.' He even claimed he was a 'Young and Dangerous' and used to run with Chen... Chen what's-his-name in Hong Kong..."

"Chen Honam?" Chen Feng said.

The stall owner nodded. "Yes, yes, yes, that's him, Chen Honam."

"And people actually believed him?" Chen Feng found it amusing.

The stall owner said, "Aiyo, those foolish kids believe him completely, trailing behind him calling him 'Big Brother.'"

Chen Feng asked, "What have these thugs been up to?"

The stall owner said, "At first they weren't too bold. Later, they got ambitious. I have a fruit stall here, and I have to pay protection money every month."

The stall owner pointed to a small restaurant at the head of the bridge. "Zhang Erwa didn't pay the protection money, so they broke into his shop in the middle of the night, carried his honeycomb briquette stoves out, and threw them into the river. They also splashed pig swill all over his walls."

"Didn't you report it to the police?" Chen Feng asked.

The stall owner sighed, "The township police station was shut down a long time ago, there's only one in the town. And that town police station only has a few people in total. When we report it, they just send two people over to investigate. They've caught a few thugs before. But those leaders of the Green Dragon Gang are always quick to hide, they can never be caught!"

"That is a difficult situation," Chen Feng said.

The stall owner said, "We're just running small businesses, and those sons of bitches carry knives and clubs. Tell me, how can we provoke them? The protection fee isn't much anyway, I only pay 10 yuan a month. Just treat it as giving money to beggars."

Chen Feng didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "10 yuan a month for a protection fee?"

"Later they said they were raising it to 15 yuan, but before I even had a chance to pay, that bunch of sons of bitches was dealt with by Chen Guiliang," the stall owner said with schadenfreude.

Chen Feng asked, "How did he deal with them?"

The stall owner said, "Chen Guiliang was cornered by them at the bridgehead after school and ran toward me in fear. He got kicked once and fell onto my fruit stall, knocking over my apples and tomatoes. Those sons of bitches surrounded him and beat him. I even saw someone hit him a couple of times with a steel pipe."

"It was summer then, and I was also selling a few watermelons. I had a watermelon knife on my stall. Chen Guiliang picked up my watermelon knife and started chopping… Reporter Chen, don't misreport this. This wasn't a brawl. The court ruled it as self-defense. In the words of TV dramas, it's 'upholding justice and eliminating evil'!"

"Chen Guiliang's homeroom teacher stepped in and wrote a petition. All of us small business owners signed and put our thumbprints on it at the time. You can ask any shop or stall owner in the market, they all signed and testified. Who wouldn't say he's a good student?"

Chen Feng had already taken out his shorthand notebook. "And then?"

When it came to the middle school female students, Chen Feng became extremely angry. "That truly is eliminating evil!"

Chen Feng then asked, "No. 2 County High is a provincial key school, how did Chen Guiliang get in?"

"He's sharp as a tack, and studies well," the stall owner said with a smile. "That bunch of sons of bitches made such a mess of the school that for two consecutive years, no student from the township got into No. 2 High. Chen Guiliang scored first in the entire township and first in the entire town that year! What's that phrase? Well-rounded in both literary and martial arts!"

The Chen Guiliang who gave his leaders and teachers headaches was a young hero in the eyes of this stall owner.

Chen Feng went to other shops and stalls to interview some self-employed individuals. They all said the thugs were scoundrels, enumerating their evil deeds, but didn't say much about Chen Guiliang.

Then he went to the school to interview Chen Guiliang's middle school teachers.

Then he went to the town police station for an interview.

Synthesizing the descriptions from all sides, the image of a teenager, excelling in both character and studies, who dared to fight against evil forces, became increasingly full-bodied.

Chen Feng recalled the preface to that poem: "Even in the humble wilderness, there exists a spirit capable of holding up the heavens and supporting the earth!"

Chen Xinghua and his wife, Yao Lan, had queued for several days in a row but couldn't get tickets home.

In the end, with no other choice, they had to pay extra for scalped tickets.

And they were standing-room-only tickets.

Carrying large and small bags of luggage, they could only stand in the carriage during the day and lie down in the aisle to nap at night. Occasionally, when someone got off mid-journey, they could seize the chance to sit for a few minutes.

They finally arrived in Shancheng, which was the final stop. They needed to transfer to another train to get back to their old hometown.

The couple's bodies ached all over, but they were reluctant to spend money on a hotel. They had only managed to buy tickets for the next day and decided to wait in the station's waiting hall for half a day and a night.

Casting aside any concern for their image, the two found a corner and spread a blanket on the floor to sleep.

Sleeping from noon until eight or nine in the evening, they finally relieved some of their fatigue. Chen Xinghua was bored and asked his wife to watch the luggage while he went outside the station to buy a few magazines.

They were all those pirated, street-stall magazines, filled with secrets, violence, and erotica.

Twenty years later, none of this content would pass review if posted on any website. At this time, however, it was sold openly and was widely popular among the lower classes.

Back in the waiting hall, Yao Lan said, "There's hot water over there."

"I'll watch our stuff, you go make some instant noodles," Chen Xinghua said, sitting down cross-legged.

Yao Lan took out two aluminum lunch boxes. Of course, they were unwilling to buy cup noodles; they always used lunch boxes to get hot water for the packet noodles.

After preparing the instant noodles, she took out two boiled eggs.

As they were eating noodles and reading magazines, some people reading a newspaper nearby started talking.

"This kid is fierce, he can get into Tsinghua or Peking University just by writing an article. And he's from our city!"

"What's that?"

"A composition contest, first prize. A reporter didn't believe he could write a good article, so he gave him a topic on the spot. The kid took seven steps and wrote another poem. You can see for yourself."

"Yo, he really is from our Longdu."

"From Fushi No. 2 High. If my kid could get recommended to Tsinghua or Peking University, I wouldn't even come back for the New Year, I'd just work my butt off every day to support his studies."

"In your dreams. Your kid, forget No. 2 High, he can't even get into No. 1 High."

"He just doesn't have it in him. Doesn't study hard, only knows how to ask for living expenses. I'm going to give him a good beating when I get back!"

"Haha, beat him after the New Year."

"…"

Hearing the words "Fushi No. 2 High," Chen Xinghua and Yao Lan simultaneously looked over. But they didn't think much of it, not assuming it was their own son.

Another migrant worker chimed in, "Hu Yaoguan, what are you guys talking about?"

"A student from Fushi No. 2 High wrote an article and got recommended to Tsinghua or Peking University."

"My nephew is also at No. 2 High, I wonder if it's him."

"Keep dreaming."

"What's his name?"

"Chen Guiliang."

Chen Xinghua and Yao Lan froze at the same time. They each put down their lunch boxes and looked at each other, confirming they hadn't misheard.

Chen Xinghua walked over and asked, "Fellow townsman, did you say Chen Guiliang from Fushi No. 2 High?"

"That's right."

"Can I borrow the newspaper to have a look?"

"Wait till I'm done reading."

"What newspaper is it?"

"Southern Weekly."

It was rare for migrant workers to read Southern Weekly.

This newspaper had been left behind in the waiting hall by someone who had finished reading it, and that migrant worker had picked it up to pass the time.

Chen Xinghua quickly ran out and soon returned with a copy, which he delightedly handed to his wife to read.

Yao Lan finished reading with a big smile on her face, then said worriedly, "Could it be someone with the same name?"

"What are the chances of such a coincidence?" Chen Xinghua said. "Liangliang has always been good at writing since he was little."

The couple read it over and over again, becoming more and more certain it was their son.

But they didn't go around announcing it, just sat there holding the newspaper, secretly happy.

More than seven years of paying off debts had made the couple cautious and discreet, never daring to be in the spotlight.

After a while, Chen Xinghua couldn't hold it in any longer. He deliberately struck up a conversation with a few migrant workers nearby, "This kid is really amazing, Tsinghua and Peking University aren't easy to get into."

One migrant worker said, "If it were my kid, I'd wake up laughing in my sleep."

Chen Xinghua said, "I'd wake up laughing too."

Another migrant worker said, "You guys can stop dreaming. A kid like this must be from the city. His mom and dad are probably teachers at some school, otherwise how could they raise him like that? Kids from the countryside just don't cut it. They're all left-behind children, fighting and causing trouble all day. Just finishing middle school makes them good students."

Chen Xinghua laughed, "That's not necessarily true, some rural kids are self-motivated too."

As they chatted, the topic shifted elsewhere.

But Chen Xinghua always managed to steer the conversation back, finding ways to induce others to praise his son.

Yao Lan watched from the side, smiling. As she smiled, her eyes grew moist.
